chapter: Baton Rouge heroes: Guy Kelly and Buddy Petit
title: Whether Joe is a New Orleans clarinet player
summary: Asked about critics who say he is not a New Orleans clarinetist, Joe notes his teachers and influence Fritz, and that many so-called New Orleans players came from elsewhere.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Let me ask you something completely out of context, but I want to get a quick reaction. Some people say you are not a New Orleans clarinet player. What do you answer to that?

Heh-heh. I don't know. The only thing I could say... The only thing I ever heard when I was a kid was New Orleans clarinet playing, and I took lessons from them. Was Picou a New Orleans clarinet player? What can you say? Maybe I didn't pick up that style exactly. One thing I can say is that I never tried to copy any of them. If anybody, it would be Fritz.

I asked that, because people have said to me these ridiculous things, about 'Oh, Joe, he's from Baton Rouge,' and they've said the same thing about Sam Lee coming from Napoleonville, and Ory coming from La Place and all that.
Good Lord, I've worked with Albert Burbank, George Lewis, Barney and all of them -- you're just as New Orleans as any of those three men.
Ed Hall didn't come from New Orleans.
No, he came from Brazil, didn't he.
That's right. Ram Hall didn't come from New Orleans. He comes from Norfolk, Louisiana. And Red
Allen didn't come from New Orleans.
If you actually look at the New Orleans Jazz scene, there's very few of them rascals did come from...

Every one of them was... That's why if they was born within 50 miles, 'I'm from New Orleans.' The average musicians (I found out when I was young) that come out of Louisiana would say they was from New Orleans.
